newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl says British election fateful for EU role.
newsitem.headline: Kohl says British election fateful for EU role.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl said on Thursday the forthcoming British general election would be a fateful one for Britain's role in Europe.

"Of course it's an important issue," Kohl told a New Year news conference. "It has to take place before the beginning of May, and so will come right in the middle of the decisive phase of negotiations for the second inter-governmental treaty (on European Union reform)."

Kohl, an enthusiastic advocate of closer political union and a single EU currency, said there were three main schools of thought in Britain on the EU -- those who wanted to quit, those who saw it as an enhanced free trade zone, and those who shared his own view.
"So it is a fateful question how Britain decides," he said. "It's a very important election, there can't be any question about that."

Last week Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel prompted accusations of foreign interference across the political spectrum in Britain when he said Britain "must reach a clear decision on its European policy", and urged it to commit itself more fully to the EU.
Some senior German politicians hope a Labour government might be more committed to the EU than the ruling Conservative Party, whose divisions on the issue are deep and public.
Some British politicians interpreted Kinkel's remarks as taking sides in an election campaign.
